## Coordinating action
Request, propose and negotiate shared or individual action.
Boundary: Require a successful request, proposal, commitment or response about action. Merely describing a desire or future event is insufficient.

Assess requests, offers or invitations, suggestions, commitments, acceptance or refusal, and negotiation. Bog an bosca seo go dtí an doras, le do thoil requests action. Ar mhaith leat cupán tae? offers tea through a preference-shaped question. Glacaimis sos proposes a shared break. Tabharfaidh mé na huirlisí liom amárach can undertake an assigned task, but future marking alone is not a promise. Ní féidir liom teacht inniu declines an invitation in context, and a Saturday alternative can negotiate the schedule. Ba mhaith can accept a prior ar mhaith question contextually. A copied le do thoil without a recoverable action is absent. Judge the actual coordinated action and participants, allowing singular or plural address appropriate to the setting. Do not confuse an offer with a neutral preference survey or require the English word let in a shared suggestion.

## Feelings and viewpoints
Express internal states, evaluations and positions.
Boundary: Require a correctly expressed feeling, desire, preference or position. An ordinary factual assertion is not automatically an opinion.

Assess desire, preference, emotion, opinion and agreement using Irish constructions. Ba mhaith liom fuáil a fhoghlaim expresses wanting to learn sewing; it is not a promise. Is fearr liom tae ná caife compares preferences with liom identifying the experiencer. Tá áthas orm faoin nuacht expresses emotion through a noun and prepositional pronoun. Ceapaim go bhfuil marks a personal judgment. Ní aontaím leis an moladh rejects a proposal. Tuigim can acknowledge comprehension without agreement. Tae can select a preferred drink contextually after a preference question; listing tea does not itself express liking. A copied maith without a recoverable stance is absent. Do not treat every assertion as opinion, demand a verb meaning like with English syntax, or confuse correct prepositional experiencer constructions with missing subjects. Judge relevant forms while allowing standard and valid dialectal alternatives.

## Information exchange
Seek, supply and verify information relevant to the exchange.
Boundary: Require successful information seeking or a relevant informative response. Question-shaped requests for action do not qualify just for their form.

Look for information questions, relevant answers, factual checks and useful detail. Cén t-am a dhúnann an siopa? asks a closing time, while Ar a cúig a chlog answers it contextually. An ndúnann an siopa ar a cúig a chlog? checks a candidate hour with a dependent interrogative form. Do not require a universal yes/no word: repeating an appropriate verb form is natural. An féidir leat cabhrú liom? normally requests help rather than merely seeking a capability report. Tá an bealach isteach taobh leis an gclós can supply a relevant landmark. A copied question particle without an intelligible question is absent. A request to repeat a word concerns conversational repair rather than an external fact. Preserve short answers and valid dialectal constructions, but do not invent the context needed to make an ambiguous fragment informative.

## Managing conversation
Establish contact, coordinate turns and repair mutual understanding.
Boundary: Require a successful opening, response, turn/topic action or repair. Sending any message or quoting a greeting does not automatically qualify.

Recognize opening or closing, acknowledgement, clarification, rephrasing, correction of misunderstanding and turn or topic management. Slán go fóill closes contact. Tuigim anois acknowledges understanding without necessarily agreement. Abair é sin arís, le do thoil requests repetition of a prior contribution. Is é sin le rá introduces reformulation. Dé Sathairn atá i gceist agam, ní Dé hAoine corrects an interpreted day. Maidir leis an gcéad cheist eile frames a topic transition. A quoted greeting in a vocabulary list is absent as conversational work. A short tuigim can acknowledge a clear explanation contextually. Do not require long sentences, invent missing antecedents or treat every new information question as repair. Judge whether the utterance manages this exchange and preserve natural mutation and prepositional constructions rather than translating an English discourse marker mechanically.

## People, things, and places
Establish referents and describe properties, locations, quantities and relationships.

Assess identification, properties, location or movement, possession or relationships, and quantity or comparison. Is í seo mo chomharsa identifies a female neighbour with the copula; Tá an tsráid seo cúng uses bí to predicate a property. Do not substitute tá directly for every copular noun identification. Ar an mbord locates an object; go dtí an doras expresses a destination. Tá dhá chathaoir agam states possession with ag and a prepositional pronoun. Dhá chathaoir counts chairs, while uimhir a dó can label a route without a quantity relation. Níos éadroime ná compares weight. Ar an mbord can answer a where-question contextually. A copied mutation or preposition with no recoverable relation is absent. Assess the actual construction and initial mutations, while recognizing valid dialectal alternatives rather than rejecting them solely for differing from a standard teaching example.

## Possibilities and constraints
Express capability, permission, requirements and epistemic limits.
Boundary: Distinguish ability, permission, obligation and likelihood. Similar wording can serve a request instead; judge the actual function.

Recognize ability, permission, necessity, possibility and certainty. Tá mé in ann snámh expresses capability. An bhfuil cead agam an mála a fhágáil anseo? explicitly asks permission, whereas is féidir constructions can concern ability or practical possibility. Caithfidh mé an eochair a thabhairt ar ais states obligation; ní gá dom removes necessity rather than forbidding action. B’fhéidir go mbeidh sé ag cur báistí presents a possible outcome. Nílim cinnte limits confidence. Tá in reply to a clear cead question can grant permission contextually. A copied modal phrase with no recoverable action is absent. A polite an féidir request does not automatically assert physical ability. Multiple plausible successful modal readings within this group are not alone grounds for unclear. Preserve the relevant prepositional pronouns, verbal-noun order and dependent verb forms without demanding an English modal-plus-bare-verb structure.

## Reasons and connections
Relate propositions through explanation, consequence, condition, contrast and support.
Boundary: Require a correctly expressed relationship between ideas. Sequence alone is not causation, a condition or an argument.

Assess causes, consequences, conditions, contrast and support for claims. Mar can introduce a reason and mar sin a consequence. Má bhíonn sé ag cur báistí amárach, fanfaimid sa bhaile establishes a condition and dependent plan. Do not impose an English word-by-word tense template on this construction. Ach contrasts properties, while ansin alone can merely sequence events. A light in a window can support an occupancy inference without causing occupancy. Mar bhí sé ag cur báistí can answer an identifiable why-question contextually. A copied connector without recoverable linked content is absent. Judge whether the evidence actually bears on the claim, whether the condition is hypothetical or asserted, and whether the chosen dependent or independent forms fit the construction. Unrelated mistakes do not erase a correctly expressed causal or conditional relationship.

## Time and events
Locate events in time and express their temporal structure.
Boundary: One correctly expressed temporal relationship is sufficient. Present properties alone do not establish temporal skill. Judge meaning in context, not a tense label.

Assess present, past and future reference, duration or recurrence, sequencing and event phase. Tá mé ag deisiú rothair describes an ongoing repair with bí and a verbal noun. Dheisigh mé an rothar inné reports a past action; deisigh has distinct past and present forms. Gheobhaidh mé na páirteanna amárach refers to a future event. Bím ag snámh describes a habit rather than merely an activity happening now. Dhá uair sa tseachtain gives recurrence; dhá uair an chloig measures duration. Ar dtús and ansin order steps; críochnaithe with a verbal noun can express having finished an activity. Inné can answer an identifiable when-question contextually. A copied time word without a recoverable event is absent. Do not credit timeless property assertions automatically, or require English perfect auxiliaries where Irish uses its own aspect constructions. Preserve genuine dialectal variants.
